[Director 指令] [Patch — 重大数值更新 + 叙事调整] D035 决策：heatmap 数据源统一为 exp_015。

**数值变更（影响 Claim 1 + 所有表格/图表）**：
- NER full: voting ρ=0.502 (旧 0.392), SJ ρ=0.357 (旧 0.383)
- Voting 显著领先 SJ（NER +0.145），不再是"统计等价"

**叙事调整方向**：
- "Structural consistency family (SJ + voting)" 仍为最强家族（远超 logprob 0.140）
- Voting 是 NER 最强单信号
- SJ 独特价值重新定位：(a) 温度鲁棒 Δρ≤0.01 (b) 泛化到任意 structured output 不限于 entity (c) conditional filtering 下 ρ=0.412 仍强 (d) 与 voting ensemble 互补 (AUROC 0.735)
- 避免说 "SJ ≈ voting"，改为 "同家族内互补，voting 更强 per-instance，SJ 更鲁棒 cross-condition"

**新增 exp-009 发现（纳入 Claim 3）**：
- SJ 在高 entity count 实例（6+）上 ρ=0.547，低 count（1-2）上 ρ=0.415
- SJ >> logprob 优势跨所有 sentence length quartile 稳定（NER Δρ≈0.08-0.20）
- 三个独立 proxy 弱相关，确认 robustness

ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

      - "NEW Cluster — Test-Time Scaling & Sample Selection (dedicated subsection): CISC (ACL Findings 2025, arXiv 2502.06233, confidence-weighted majority vote), Self-Certainty BoN (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2502.18581, KL-divergence selection), ReASC (arXiv 2601.02970, adaptive sampling), Ranked Voting SC (arXiv 2505.10772), Latent SC (arXiv 2508.18395). KEY FRAMING: ALL operate on reasoning/QA with discrete answer spaces. We are FIRST to (a) extend SC to set-valued structured outputs (IE), (b) discover correlation-selection gap: strong quality estimation ↛ selection ability. Self-Certainty BoN is direct academic dialogue: they demonstrate reward-free selection works for reasoning; we show it FAILS for structured IE NER."
      - "NEW Cluster — Consistency for Structured IE (dedicated subsection): Nédellec & Xia (Genomics Informatics, 2026-02, PMC12888769) — most direct competitor: consistency-accuracy correlation in hard-prompted LLMs for NER/RE on plant-health data. CoCoA (Vashurin et al., NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2502.04964) — MBR framework fusing confidence+consistency for UQ on QA/summarization/translation, parallels our exp-016 ensemble but not structured IE. Vashurin et al. (arXiv 2510.20460, 2025) — systematic evaluation of 4 UQ methods (VCE/MSP/SC/CoCoA), tasks exclude structured IE. FRAMING: Nédellec & Xia's surface-matching limitation motivates SJ; CoCoA's confidence+consistency fusion parallels our ensemble analysis; both confirm structured IE as underexplored."
      - "Cluster 2 — Uncertainty estimation & calibration: Kuhn 2023 semantic uncertainty, Semantic Entropy Probes (arXiv 2406.15927), Kadavath 2022 P(True), Guo 2017, Desai & Durrett 2020 → we compare model confidence with output-space consistency"

      - "Cluster 8 — IE confidence & selective prediction: Culotta & McCallum 2004, Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017, Jagannatha & Yu 2022 → pre-LLM approaches"

  - section: method
    word_budget: 1000
    core_bullets:
      - "Problem formulation: given LLM M, input x, N stochastic samples {y_1,...,y_N}, define confidence signal c(x, {y_i}) → ℝ"
      - "Signal 1 — Log-probability: c_lp(y_i) = (1/|y_i|) Σ log p(t_j|t_{<j}, x). Per-sample signal. Clarify: sequence-level mean, not token-level max."
      - "Signal 2 — Exact-match voting: c_em(x) = max_y |{i: y_i = y}| / N. Instance-level."
      - "Signal 3 — Fleiss' Kappa (FK): token-level inter-rater agreement. Instance-level."
      - "Signal 4 — Soft Jaccard (SJ): set-aware structural similarity via type-grouped bipartite matching. Instance-level. Key: uses Hungarian matching with max(|A|,|B|) normalization."
      - "Signal 5 — Entity voting confidence: per-entity majority voting rate, averaged. Instance-level."
      - "Distinction: log-prob is PER-SAMPLE (ranks candidates), others are INSTANCE-LEVEL (aggregate across samples). This distinction is central to the correlation-selection gap."
      - "Evaluation: quality estimation (ρ, τ, AUROC vs F1) and sample selection (best-of-N F1)"

    notation_table:
      M: "language model"

      y_i: "i-th stochastic sample"
      N: "number of samples"

      SJ: "soft Jaccard similarity"
      FK: "Fleiss' Kappa"

  - section: experiments
    word_budget: 2400
    subsections:
      - name: setup
        word_budget: 500
        core_bullets:
          - "Datasets: SciERC (science, 551 test, NER+RE joint), CoNLL-2003 (news, 3453 test, NER), WNUT-17 (social media, NER — method boundary analysis)"
          - "Model: Qwen3-8B fine-tuned with LoRA (r=32) per dataset. LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct for cross-model validation (exp_007)."
          - "Sampling: N=8 primary, N=16 for scaling analysis. T=1.0 standard, T=0.7 for robustness."
          - "Evaluation: greedy F1 as reference, per-instance F1 vs each signal's ρ/τ/AUROC, best-of-N selection F1"
          - "Implementation: vLLM inference, XGrammar constrained decoding, span realignment post-processing"

      - name: quality_estimation
        word_budget: 600
        core_bullets:
          - "Table 1: All 5 signals × {SciERC NER, SciERC RE, CoNLL NER} × {ρ, τ, AUROC}"
          - "SciERC NER: voting 0.704 ≈ SJ 0.689 >> FK 0.629 ≈ EM 0.640 >> logprob 0.591 (AUROC)"
          - "CoNLL NER: EM 0.816 > SJ 0.801 > EV 0.789 > FK 0.774 > logprob 0.753 — EM > SJ on easy task!"
          - "SciERC RE: voting 0.667 > FK 0.626 ≈ logprob 0.619 > SJ 0.592 > EM 0.586 — degraded"
          - "Key: structural consistency family dominates on hard tasks, EM dominates on easy tasks"
        registry_refs: [mvp_pilot_004, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_013_exact_match_voting, exp_014_entity_majority_voting, exp_015_metrics_expansion, exp_002]
        tables: [tab_quality_estimation]

      - name: correlation_selection_gap
        word_budget: 600
        core_bullets:
          - "Table 2: Best-of-N selection F1 for each signal vs greedy vs oracle"
          - "NER: greedy 0.609 ≥ ALL signals (logprob 0.609, SJ 0.604, voting 0.596). Oracle 0.769 (+16pp headroom)"
          - "RE: logprob 0.397 > greedy 0.374 (+2.4pp). SJ 0.368, voting 0.338 ≈ random. Oracle 0.561 (+18.7pp)"
          - "CoNLL: voting 0.914 > greedy 0.912 (+0.18pp) — first instance where voting beats greedy, on easy task"
          - "Explanation: instance-level signals predict WHICH INPUTS are reliable, not WHICH OUTPUTS are best. Only per-sample logprob can rank candidates."
          - "Ensemble analysis: SJ+voting NER ρ=0.489 (+23%), AUROC 0.735 (+3.5pp). But ensemble SELECTION still fails."
        registry_refs: [exp_016_signal_ensemble, exp_002]
        tables: [tab_selection]
        figures: [fig_selection_gap]

      - name: task_complexity
        word_budget: 400
        core_bullets:
          - "Signal ranking shifts with task difficulty: CoNLL (easy, F1=0.91) EM>SJ; SciERC NER (hard, F1=0.66) SJ>EM; SciERC RE (harder) all signals degrade"
          - "RE diagnostic: FEATURE-OF near-zero ρ, HYPONYM-OF ρ=0.65. Entity span errors = 55.5% of RE FN."
          - "Fisher z-test: NER ρ_sj significantly > RE ρ_sj (p=0.021)"
          - "Compound error propagation: head_sj ρ=0.21 (vs NER 0.38) — fundamental, not formula issue"
        registry_refs: [exp_004_re_diagnostic, e1_component_wise_re_sj, exp_002]

      - name: analysis
        word_budget: 300
        core_bullets:
          - "Temperature robustness: SJ Δρ=±0.01 across T=0.7/1.0; FK Δρ=0.06-0.09; logprob most sensitive (Δρ=0.17)"
          - "N-scaling: N=8→16 NER flat (saturated), RE voting improves 0.340→0.380"
          - "LOO-SJ: Δρ=-0.014, evaluation circularity minimal"
          - "Conditional filtering: RE cond SJ ρ=0.37 (full 0.24) — separating knowledge-gap errors critical"
          - "Cross-model: LLaMA-3.1-8B confirms SJ>FK on NER (ρ 0.363 vs 0.327), RE cond SJ recovers (0.405 vs 0.259). Pattern model-agnostic."
        registry_refs: [exp_005, exp_001_ner_n16_scierc, exp_015_metrics_expansion, exp_007_llama_inference]
        figures: [fig_signal_heatmap]

      - name: method_boundary
        word_budget: 400
        core_bullets:
          - "D029: WNUT-17 as method boundary analysis — When Does Structural Consistency Fail?"
          - "WNUT-17 SJ ρ=0.082 near-zero. Root cause: training data 63.8% empty instances (vs SciERC 0%), model learns strong empty-output prior"
          - "16/16 samples all empty → SJ=1.0 but F1=0, systematically inflates consistency for wrong predictions"
          - "Logprob also fails: empty predictions get logprob=-0.007 (extreme high confidence), ρ=-0.41 (anti-correlated)"
          - "Conditional filtering partially helps: post-filter logprob ρ=+0.35, but SJ remains weak"
          - "Conclusion: SJ effectiveness requires model to have basic task competence — degenerate training data (>50% empty) invalidates all unsupervised signals"
          - "This is NOT a dataset limitation but a method boundary: identifies preconditions for structural consistency"
        registry_refs: [exp_003_wnut17_eval]

    registry_refs: [mvp_pilot_004, mvp_pilot_005, exp_001_ner_n16_scierc, exp_002, exp_004_re_diagnostic, exp_005, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_013_exact_match_voting, exp_014_entity_majority_voting, exp_015_metrics_expansion, exp_016_signal_ensemble, e1_component_wise_re_sj, exp_007_llama_inference, exp_003_wnut17_eval]

  - section: discussion
    word_budget: 500
    core_bullets:
      - "When WOULD consistency help: (a) poor calibration (ICL without fine-tuning), (b) closed-source APIs (no logprob), (c) ensemble/mixture settings, (d) systematically overconfident models"
      - "Non-obviousness of negative result: self-consistency works for reasoning (+18pp GSM8K), structured prediction has rich internal structure, the DEGREE of gap and task-complexity boundary are not predictable a priori"
      - "Practical recommendations: quality estimation → structural consistency; best-of-N → logprob (RE only); NER → greedy is near-optimal"
      - "Conditional analysis as unique contribution: separating knowledge-gap errors (RE ~44% zero-F1, WNUT-17 ~64% empty) reveals hidden signal value — SJ recovers on RE cond (Δ=0.15-0.21 over FK)"
      - "Limitations: 1 RE dataset (SciERC), 2 model families (Qwen3 + LLaMA), no supervised upper bound beyond logistic regression proxy"
    dependencies: [experiments]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 300
    core_bullets:
      - "Summary: first systematic comparison of confidence signals for quality estimation vs selection in generative IE"
      - "Three findings: (1) structural consistency best for quality estimation, (2) correlation-selection gap, (3) task-complexity boundary"
      - "Future work: supervised verifiers, cross-task transfer of confidence signals, conformal prediction integration, scaling to larger models"
    dependencies: [experiments, discussion]

visualization_plan:
  - fig_id: fig_overview
    type: conceptual
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >
      Overview figure (1-column) illustrating the paper's core finding. Left: quality estimation
      (consistency signals predict which instances are reliable). Right: sample selection (the same
      signals fail to pick the best sample). Shows the conceptual distinction between instance-level
      and per-sample signals. Simple schematic with boxes and arrows — not a full architecture diagram.
    placement: introduction
    aspect_ratio: "2:1"
    data_source: "manual"

  - fig_id: fig_selection_gap
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >
      Two-panel figure. Left panel: grouped bar chart of AUROC for quality estimation (5 signals,
      SciERC NER). Right panel: grouped bar chart of best-of-N selection F1 (same 5 signals + greedy
      + oracle, SciERC NER + RE). Horizontal dashed line at greedy F1. Visualizes the gap: high AUROC
      does NOT translate to high selection F1. Include error bars from bootstrap CI where available.
    data_source: "registry: exp_016_signal_ensemble, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_014_entity_majority_voting"
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "2:1"

  - fig_id: fig_signal_heatmap
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >
      Heatmap (signals as rows, datasets/tasks as columns) showing Spearman ρ values. Columns:
      SciERC NER (N=8), SciERC RE (N=8), CoNLL NER (N=8). Rows: voting_conf, SJ, EM, FK, logprob.
      Color-coded from red (low) to green (high). Annotated with ρ values. Visualizes task-complexity
      boundary: signal ranking shifts across columns.
    data_source: "registry: mvp_pilot_004, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_013_exact_match_voting, exp_014_entity_majority_voting, exp_002"
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "4:3"

  - fig_id: fig_reliability
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >
      Reliability diagram (2 panels: NER, RE). For each signal, bin instances by predicted confidence
      (decile), plot mean predicted confidence vs mean actual F1. Perfect calibration = diagonal.
      Shows which signals are well-calibrated vs overconfident. Focus on SJ, voting_conf, logprob (3 curves per panel).
    caption_notes: >
      Caption or surrounding text MUST note two definition differences:
      (1) F1 definition: y-axis uses mean_sample_f1 (average F1 across N stochastic samples per instance),
      distinct from greedy F1 used in Table 1 ρ/AUROC targets — this is the calibration-appropriate measure
      since confidence signals aggregate over stochastic samples.
      (2) Logprob normalization: logprob is globally min-max normalized to [0,1] (SJ and voting_conf are
      naturally [0,1]). ECE absolute values are therefore NOT directly comparable across signals — only
      relative calibration patterns (over/under-confident regions) are meaningful.
    data_source: "registry: mvp_pilot_004, exp_012_logprob_baseline, exp_014_entity_majority_voting"
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "2:1"

**N=16 NER（exp-001v2, 2 seeds）**：
- SJ full ρ: 0.428/0.424（seed42/123），cross-seed Δ<0.01 极稳定
- 对比 N=8 (exp_015): SJ 0.357→0.428 (+0.071)，FK 0.265→0.281 (+0.016)
- **SJ scaling 增益远大于 FK**——支持"结构信号随 N 增长增强"的叙事

- RE full: logprob ρ=0.287 > SJ ρ=0.281 ≈ FK 0.279（三者持平，logprob 微幅领先）
- RE cond: SJ ρ=0.308 vs logprob ρ=-0.026 (p=0.685，完全失效)
- **不能笼统说"结构信号全面优于 logprob"**

**建议叙事**：
- NER: 结构信号（voting/SJ）全面领先，SJ 随 N scaling 增益显著
- RE full: 所有信号持平（compound error propagation 的天花板效应）
- RE cond: 结构信号独特价值——剔除知识盲区后 SJ 仍有效 (0.308)，而 logprob 完全崩溃 (-0.026)
- 统一框架："结构信号在 model capability range 内是最强质量估计器；超出此范围所有信号趋同"

    entity voting leads (ρ=0.50, AUROC 0.73) with soft Jaccard as complementary robust signal
    (temperature-invariant Δρ≤0.01, conditional filtering ρ=0.41). A correlation-selection gap means
    this does not translate to best-of-N selection — no signal beats greedy on NER, only logprob helps
    on RE (+2.4pp). Signal effectiveness is task-difficulty-dependent: easy tasks favor exact-match,
    hard tasks favor structural consistency, and SJ strength scales with instance complexity (entity count 6+ ρ=0.55).
